simplemodels.browser.title: Simple Models
simplemodels.browser.tab_hint: Browse and assign server-approved item models
simplemodels.browser.search: Search name, item, author, or tag
simplemodels.browser.assign_hint: Select the model, then take the result from the anvil. Server rules and level costs apply.
simplemodels.browser.empty: No approved models match. Ask the server administrator to add definitions and reload the catalog.
simplemodels.browser.import: Add or remove JSON definitions in config/simplemodels/catalogue on the server, then run /simplemodels reload. Put rendering assets in an enabled folder resource pack (assets/<namespace>/items, models, textures). Reload Assets refreshes previews. Multiplayer servers distribute assets with the standard server resource pack URL and SHA-1 settings; never share private files. Assignment requires an anvil and an empty second slot. Model changes do not change item names or stats. Server Settings is read-only; admins edit config/simplemodels/config.json. See docs/modules/simplemodels.md for the JSON format.
simplemodels.config.enabled.tooltip:
Allow cosmetic model changes at anvils.
Default: true.
simplemodels.config.operatorsOnly.toolti:
Only operators with game master permission
may assign or remove models. Default: true.
simplemodels.config.allowModItems.toolti:
Allow explicitly approved mod items; gameplay
components remain unchanged. Default: false.
simplemodels.config.legacyNameMatching.t:
Also accept exact match_name text at anvils.
No suffix matching or hidden identity.
Default: false.
simplemodels.config.levelCost.tooltip:
Levels charged by the vanilla anvil per model
change, capped at 1–10. Default: 1.
simplemodels.config.maxModels.tooltip:
Approved definitions, capped at 1–64 and
24,000 serialized characters. Default: 64.
simplemodels.config.maxFileBytes.tooltip:
JSON definition bytes, capped at 256–16384.
Invalid, nested, or oversized files are
rejected. Default: 16384.
simplemodels.guide.page.1.title: Simple Models
simplemodels.guide.page.1: Server-approved custom item models, anvil assignment and a searchable model browser.
simplemodels.guide.page.2.title: Anvil Assignment
simplemodels.guide.page.2: Put an approved base item in the left anvil slot, leave the second slot empty, choose Models, then Assign and take the result. Only item_model changes; names, enchantments, counts, durability, and other components remain intact.

simplemodels.guide.page.11.title: Multiplayer Safety
simplemodels.guide.page.11: The server owns the catalog and policy. It syncs definitions to clients; clients cannot
simplemodels.guide.page.12.title: Multiplayer Safety
simplemodels.guide.page.12: upload models or select an arbitrary item_model. Default operator-only assignment. Disabling assignment refuses new changes;
simplemodels.guide.page.13.title: Multiplayer Safety
simplemodels.guide.page.13: existing saved cosmetic components remain. No hidden item identity, automatic downloads, arbitrary file paths, or gameplay stats.
simplemodels.guide.page.14.title: Legacy renamed Compatibility
simplemodels.guide.page.14: No item/block/entity/enchantment registries existed in renamed. Definition fields id, base_item, match_name, model, tags, author remain readable; bare ids use the renamed namespace.
simplemodels.guide.page.15.title: Legacy renamed Compatibility
simplemodels.guide.page.15: Optional exact legacy anvil name matching preserves custom names. The old unsafe bracket-hiding/render mixins are replaced by item_model. No new items, blocks, mobs, recipes, loot, advancements, or keybinds are added.
simplemodels.guide.page.16.title: Legacy renamed Compatibility
simplemodels.guide.page.16: Block-item appearances are supported; placed block geometry is not changed.
simplemodels.guide.page.17.title: /simplemodels reload
simplemodels.guide.page.17: Game master permission is required. Rescan the server folder and policy, then synchronize the new catalog to connected players. Add/remove files without restarting.
simplemodels.guide.page.18.title: /simplemodels reload
simplemodels.guide.page.18: Malformed policy disables assignment; bad definitions are skipped with server logs.
